name: Highlands 25

alpha.desc: The alpha view shows the front of the property from a distance, revealing a large, sparsely vegetated lot on sloped terrain with scattered juniper-type trees across the hillside|The residence is visible near the center of the lot, partially obscured by surrounding trees, with light-colored roofing distinguishable among the vegetation|The approach to the structure traverses open, sandy-gravelly terrain with scattered tree cover that would allow vehicle movement but no defined improved road is visible from this angle|The overall elevation change from the front of the parcel down toward the structure is gradual.

bravo.desc: The bravo view shows the property from the right side, with the residence visible near the upper-center of the frame as a light-colored structure set amid scattered conifer trees on open desert terrain|The right side of the parcel is largely open and undeveloped, with sparse tree coverage and sandy, open ground providing potential lateral access on foot|No fencing, gates, or outbuildings are visible on the right side of the property|The terrain on the right side appears relatively flat to gently sloping.

charlie.desc: The charlie view shows the rear of the property, where the residence is visible in the upper-left portion of the frame as a low-profile light-colored structure|The rear yard is open and largely undeveloped, with scattered conifer trees across sandy, arid terrain extending a considerable distance behind the structure|No fencing, outbuildings, or hardscaped features are visible at the rear|The open rear terrain provides unobstructed foot access around the back of the structure.

delta.desc: The delta view shows the left side of the property, where the residence and what appears to be a detached structure or garage are visible as white-roofed buildings partially surrounded by trees|The left side of the parcel has a higher density of conifer trees compared to the other sides, which limits sightlines and creates screening between the road and the structure|A driveway or access path is visible cutting through the trees toward the structure from the left side|The tree density on this side would require responders to navigate around or between trees to reach the structure.

considerations: The residence sits on a large, rural lot with a long approach driveway from the adjacent road, and the structure is set back significantly from the street with scattered juniper-type trees that reduce direct sightlines from the roadway. The terrain is open and arid with sandy, firm-appearing ground, which may support off-road vehicle movement around most of the structure's perimeter. No fencing or gates are visible that would restrict perimeter access, and the rear and right sides of the property are open and accessible on foot. Tree density is highest on the left (driveway) side of the property, which may limit visibility and vehicle clearance in that approach corridor.
clarifications: Is the driveway surface improved (paved or compacted gravel) and capable of supporting the weight of a fire apparatus or ambulance for its full length to the residence? Are there any gates, barriers, or access controls along the driveway that are not visible from aerial imagery? Does the detached structure visible on the left side serve as a garage, and does it have an interior vehicle bay? Are there any propane tanks, fuel storage, or other hazardous materials stored on the property that are not visible from overhead? What is the designated address number display location and is it visible from the road approach?
